# Gaussian and Primitive-Based Representations

Also called: Discrete Primitive Representations, Point-Based Neural Rendering, Gaussian Splatting Variants

## Overview
Gaussian and Primitive-Based Representations replace the continuous, query-based Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) function of standard NeRF with discrete 3D structures (Gaussians, points, or quadric primitives) to improve rendering speed and geometric efficiency [13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md][14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md][15538-point-nerf-representation.md][15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md]. This family solves the computational bottleneck of ray marching through empty space and the spectral bias of MLPs, offering faster per-scene optimization and real-time inference capabilities [15538-point-nerf-representation.md][15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md]. Unlike the continuous implicit functions in [Model Architecture Modifications](11313-model-architecture-modifications.md), these methods explicitly model scene geometry and appearance using localized primitives, differing from siblings like [Voxel and Sparse Grid Representations](13738-voxel-and-sparse-grid-representations.md) by using non-grid-aligned, often anisotropic or point-based, discrete elements [13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md][15538-point-nerf-representation.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family substitute the global continuous function $f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ with a discrete set of primitives $\mathcal{P} = \{p_i\}_{i=1}^N$. The rendering process involves:
1.  **Discretization:** The scene is represented by a finite set of elements (Gaussians, points, or quadrics) with learnable parameters (position, covariance, color, opacity, or implicit shape parameters).
2.  **Local Query/Projection:** Instead of querying a global MLP at arbitrary points, the method either projects 3D primitives to 2D screen space (Gaussian Splatting) or aggregates local features from neighboring primitives (Point-NeRF) or evaluates implicit distances (DPA).
3.  **Differentiable Rendering:** The final pixel color is computed via alpha compositing or volume rendering, ensuring gradients flow back to the primitive parameters:
    $$
    C(\mathbf{p}) = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} \mathbf{c}_i \alpha_i \prod_{j=1}^{i-1} (1 - \alpha_j)
    $$
    where $\mathcal{N}$ is the set of primitives contributing to pixel $\mathbf{p}$, sorted by depth.
4.  **Optimization:** Parameters are optimized using image-space losses (e.g., $\mathcal{L}_{ph}$) and auxiliary losses specific to the representation (e.g., selection loss for DPA, frequency modulation for AFNet).

## Subtopics

### [Differentiable Primitive Assembly](13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md)
Differentiable Primitive Assembly (DPA) models 3D shapes as an assembly of quadric primitives using differentiable intersection and union operations, trained with image-space losses only without 3D supervision [13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md]. It differs from its sibling [Viewing Direction Gaussian Splatting](14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md) by representing geometry via implicit quadric surfaces grouped into convexes, rather than explicit anisotropic Gaussians [13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md]. It is chosen when explicit geometric topology (convexes) is required or when dealing with complex shapes where Gaussian splatting might suffer from aliasing or transparency artifacts.

### [Viewing Direction Gaussian Splatting](14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md)
Viewing Direction Gaussian Splatting (VDGS) is a hybrid neural rendering method that combines the geometric efficiency of 3D Gaussian Splatting (GS) with the view-dependent appearance modeling of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) [14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md]. While standard GS represents scene geometry and static color using discrete 3D Gaussians, VDGS introduces a neural network to modulate the opacity (and optionally color) of these Gaussians based on the viewing direction [14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md]. This approach solves the limitation of standard GS in rendering view-dependent effects such as glass reflections, transparency, and specular highlights, which static Gaussian attributes cannot capture [14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md]. Unlike classical GS where color and opacity are fixed per Gaussian, VDGS achieves view sensitivity without a notable increase in training time compared to standard GS, inheriting the fast inference speeds of rasterization while maintaining the quality of MLP-based renderers [14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [Point-NeRF Representation](15538-point-nerf-representation.md)
Point-NeRF is a volumetric neural rendering method that represents a scene as a discrete neural point cloud rather than a continuous implicit function, avoiding ray sampling in empty space by leveraging classical point clouds to approximate scene geometry [15538-point-nerf-representation.md]. It differs from its siblings by using a PointNet-like architecture to regress volume density and view-dependent radiance from local neighborhoods of neural points, enabling faster per-scene optimization than standard NeRF while maintaining high reconstruction quality [15538-point-nerf-representation.md]. It is suitable for scenes with sparse geometry or when memory efficiency is prioritized over the dense rasterization of Gaussians.

### [Frequency-Modulated Point Cloud Rendering](15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md)
Frequency-Modulated Point Cloud Rendering is a pipeline that renders scenes from a discrete point cloud representation using an Adaptive Frequency Net (AFNet) to modulate implicit radiance signals with local texture frequency encoding [15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md]. It solves the problem of high-frequency detail reconstruction in point-based rendering, where standard MLPs suffer from spectral bias towards low-frequency signals [15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md]. Unlike its siblings, it decouples frequency adaptation from the global network by using a hypernetwork to predict per-point frequency and phase parameters, enabling real-time rendering (39.27 FPS on NeRF-Synthetic) and direct point cloud editing [15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md]. It is 1700× faster than NeRF and 37× faster than CCNeRF [15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md].

### GARF
#### definition
GARF uses Gaussian activations as an effective alternative to positional encoding in NeRF, in conjunction with bundle adjustment for pose estimation [S1]. It successfully recovers scene representations from unknown camera poses, even in challenging scenes with low-textured regions, making it suitable for real-world applications [S1].

#### step
1.  Use Gaussian activations as an effective alternative to positional encoding [S1].
2.  Perform bundle adjustment for pose estimation [S1].

#### number
GARF successfully recovers scene representations from unknown camera poses in challenging scenes with low-textured regions [S1].

## Background
The shift from continuous MLPs to discrete primitives was driven by the need for faster training and rendering speeds in Neural Radiance Fields. Standard NeRF [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) requires extensive ray sampling and MLP queries, which is computationally expensive. Early works like Point-NeRF [15538-point-nerf-representation.md] and Gaussian Splatting variants [14273-viewing-direction-gaussian-splatting.md] leveraged the efficiency of rasterization and explicit geometry. Differentiable Primitive Assembly [13657-differentiable-primitive-assembly.md] introduced implicit quadrics for better geometric fidelity. Frequency-Modulated Point Cloud Rendering [15903-frequency-modulated-point-cloud-rendering.md] addressed the spectral bias of MLPs in point-based methods. GARF [S1] explored Gaussian activations for pose estimation in SLAM contexts. These methods are widely used in real-time rendering, AR/VR, and large-scale scene reconstruction where speed and memory efficiency are critical.
